why: On 2026-09-06 public/interop/agent-card-jws-input.json described a card nobody served. Its producer was correct; nothing re-ran it. The whole gates job was red for every lane until someone noticed. This manifest names source -> producer -> output so CI can notice instead.
how_to_read: Each entry names what a producer WRITES and how to prove the committed bytes still match. `gated: true` entries are enforced by scripts/producers-check.mjs in CI. `gated: false` entries record WHY they cannot be, which is the more useful half. Two of the three x402-census entries carry `becomes_gated_when` instead of `gated: true`: their --check has nothing to compare until a second round exists, and a check that cannot fail is not a gate. Their `selftest` command runs on every PR instead, and that is the half that can go red today.
extending: Add an entry, run `node scripts/producers-check.mjs` locally, and only set gated:true once it passes on a clean tree. Never set gated:true on a producer that stamps a timestamp or a random id into its output, and never on one that signs.

producers.reason: Reads another GIT BRANCH: `git show os-production:<path>` and `git diff origin/master...os-production`. The gates job uses actions/checkout@v4 with no fetch-depth, i.e. a depth-1 SINGLE-BRANCH clone, so origin/os-production does not exist there and the script exits non-zero. It passes on a developer clone, which has every branch — that difference is exactly why it was wrongly gated first.
producers.do_not_fix_by: Adding fetch-depth: 0 to make this one step pass. That slows every CI run for every lane to satisfy one gate, and gates are never widened to make a tip deployable. Gate it in the harness lane's own workflow, where the branch is already fetched.

producers.reason: The per-cell mill evidence lives as 664 items-<axis>-<hash>.jsonl files whose NAME carries only a truncated axis and a content hash — the model is inside the file. A consumer cannot find a cell for a given model without opening every file, cannot join the cells without reading all of them, and cannot read the corpus as a table. This producer joins the cells into one long fact table (model, axis, item, outcome), the item universe it refers to, and an index of the cells it came from. It copies no number it did not read, and it says how many rows carry no model and no grade rather than dropping them.
producers.outputs_note: The measurements table is written in PARTS and the MANIFEST names them (tables.measurements.parts), so the parts are a function of the corpus size and cannot be listed here one by one. The producer's own --check compares every part against a fresh build, which is the check that runs in CI; the list above names the first part and the two single-file tables.
